$\text{Slope}=\dfrac{\text{Rise}}{\text{Run}}=\dfrac{\text{Change in }y}{\text{Change in }x}$

We can calculate the change in $x$ and change in $y$ by picking any two pairs of corresponding $x$- and $y$-values.

$\begin{array}{lrrrr}
&&\xrightarrow{+2}\,\,\,\,
&\xrightarrow{+2}\,\,\,\,
&\xrightarrow{+2}\,\,\,\,
\\
x
&15
&17
&19
&21
\\
\hline
\\
y
&-10
&2
&14
&26
\\
&&\xrightarrow[+12]{}\,\,\,\,
&\xrightarrow[+12]{}\,\,\,\,
&\xrightarrow[+12]{}\,\,\,\,
\end{array}$

So the slope is:

$\dfrac{\text{Change in }y}{\text{Change in }x}=\dfrac{12}{2}=6$
